chapter: First big band, his father, arriving in Kansas City
title: Hearing Jimmy Rushing sing a waltz, probably with the Blue Devils
summary: He recalls a band with Jimmy Rushing singing 'When the Leaves Bid the Trees Goodbye', and he and Stanley conclude it was probably the original Blue Devils, not Moten.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: I'm pretty sure that was his first trip, too. He might have heard them before, but I know this was really my first trip. Now, I had heard Clarence Love, you know, like when I was in school down there. But see, now, when I was around home, the folks didn't let me go out to no dances or anything like that, see, so I didn't get a chance to catch Benny -- I caught Benny Moten one time. Was it Benny? I thought it was Benny because -- I do know this, that Jimmy Rushing was with the band. That's the reason I assumed it was Benny Moten's band.
It wasn't Walter Page's Blue Devils?
Well, that could have been. That could have been, because Jimmy Rushing -- I remember --he sang with a megaphone and you know, a megaphone they put up to their mouth and sing through it?
Yeah.

And the song that he'd sing, even out of all the blues and stuff that he did that night, the thing that impressed me most was a waltz that he sang and the waltz was -- the name of that waltz was When the Leaves Bid the Trees Good-bye.1)
Say it again?
When the Leaves Bid the Trees Good-bye. 1)
I don't know that one.
I still play it today when I get a request for a waltz, you know.
You remember it?

Still remember it. I liked it and he sang it, but it was some kind of way that he was slurring those notes that really -- I loved so well and the slurring the notes on a waltz, you know, and -- (Laughter.) -- and I always remembered it. Never did forget it.
I don't think I ever heard Jimmy Rushing sing a waltz.
How about that? Yes, that --
Well, of course, in those days, the waltzes were played must more.
Oh, yes. They were played more. That's true. And -- but with the exception of that group, this was the first big band I had heard. I had heard small groups like Clarence Love and like that. But --
Well, now, I was just trying to think, you know, if you hear Benny Moten's records, old ones, you know, they're not very good. But then when you get Basie
and Walter Page in there, the whole thing changes. The rhythm section is good and --
And then from what I understand now, the band that we mentioned a while ago that we assumed it must have been --
The original Blue Devils.
The original Blue Devils. I'm sure that must have been the original Blue Devils, because they didn't sound like Benny Moten.
No.

The only reason I assumed in later years that it was Benny Moten was because Rush was there and I didn't forget Rush. I just -- you know, some things that you just don't forget. And I was so impressed with that.
Yeah. Well, I know they made only one record. But it was pretty good.
Yes.
It was better than Benny Moten's.
